PullRequest.Title: ci: Parallelize integration and smoke test shards
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

- run Agent Host E2E in conditional platform jobs beside the remaining Electron integration tests
- split Electron smoke coverage into complementary core and chat shards on Linux, macOS, and Windows
- move the macOS PAC and Kerberos proxy scenarios off the main Electron smoke critical path
- skip repeated prelaunch synchronization in already-prepared test jobs
- avoid compiling Copilot for Browser smoke jobs, which do not register Chat or Agents Window suites
- skip login-shell environment probing for deterministic Browser and Remote test servers
- use Mocha's Dot console reporter for Browser unit tests while preserving full JUnit results

## Measured impact

Using #334766 and this PR's first Code OSS attempt as baselines:

- the initial test sharding moved Agent Host E2E and chat/proxy smoke work off the main Electron paths
- Browser test servers currently repeat prelaunch synchronization 17-18 times per job
- a focused Browser smoke run took 15.4s with prelaunch and 12.2s without it, projecting roughly 50-60s saved per Browser job
- the Browser unit reporter benchmark reduced output from 2,761 to 263 lines and from 177KB to 80KB for the same 2,700-test subset, with identical JUnit coverage
- Browser-only Copilot compilation removes another 5-8s of unnecessary work

The remaining major setup opportunity is dependency caching: Windows downloads its 1.2GB node_modules cache in about 10s but spends about 71s extracting 6.6GB / 223k files. `extensions/copilot/node_modules` alone accounts for 1.28GB and 74k files, so job-specific additive caches could remove another 20-30s from Browser jobs, but that needs coordinated cache seeding and is intentionally not mixed into this change.

## Validation

- parsed the root and reusable workflows and asserted caller inputs, check names, artifact uniqueness, prelaunch settings, and Browser-only compile conditions
- focused Browser smoke run: passed in 12.2s
- focused Remote smoke run: passed in 15.7s
- Browser unit benchmark: 2,700 tests passed with the Dot and JUnit reporters
- compiled `test/integration/browser`
- compiled `test/automation`
- compiled `vscode-test-resolver`
- targeted ESLint for all changed JavaScript and TypeScript files
- `node --check test/smoke/test/index.js`
- `git diff --check`
- `npm ci`

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The move from in-job execution to three new reusable-workflow invocations and the unconditional transitive setup steps are explicit. Exact queue delay depends on runner availability, but the added work and its three-platform cardinality are certain.
Findings.PerformanceResource: three additional runners performing checkout, dependency-cache extraction, full transpilation, Electron download, and filesystem/network I/O
Findings.PerformanceScaling: For every PR classified as Agent Host-affecting, the cost is repeated once on each of Linux, macOS, and Windows; the classifier includes broad prefixes such as `build/`, `src/vs/base/`, and `src/vs/platform/`, so this is not limited to changes in the E2E tests themselves.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: increased runner-minutes and boundary I/O, with lower aggregate CI throughput and additional shared-pool queue pressure
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Agent Host E2E ran from each existing Electron integration job after that job had already restored dependencies, transpiled the client and extensions, and downloaded Electron; unaffected changes skipped the suite in place.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The integration jobs now always skip Agent Host E2E, while each affected platform starts a separate full reusable workflow whose only enabled test is Agent Host E2E, repeating all unconditional preparation solely to move the suite beside the integration job.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added reusable-workflow call at `.github/workflows/pr.yml:153` creates a dedicated Linux job, with equivalent added calls for macOS and Windows. The diff simultaneously changes each original integration workflow to `VSCODE_SKIP_AGENT_HOST_E2E: '1'`, proving the test execution was moved out of an already-prepared job into three newly prepared jobs.
Findings.Title: Avoid rebuilding each platform just to extract Agent Host E2E
Findings.Impact: A realistic platform or build change now causes three extra full repository preparations before the same three platform suites run. Parallel execution can shorten that PR's longest check, but the duplicated CPU, cache traffic, and Electron downloads consume additional shared CI capacity and reduce throughput for concurrent PRs.
Findings.Evidence: Following this call into the platform workflows shows that `unit_tests`, `integration_tests`, and `smoke_tests` being false does not bypass checkout, node_modules cache download/extraction (or install), built-in-extension cache access, `transpile-client-esbuild transpile-extensions`, or Electron download. Only after all of those boundaries does `scripts/test-agent-host-e2e.ts` run. Previously that script was reached from the already-prepared Electron integration job, so the diff adds three complete setup passes whenever detection returns true.
Findings.Recommendation: Keep Agent Host E2E parallel, but fan the integration and E2E test jobs out from one prepared build artifact per platform, or otherwise make the dedicated E2E workflow consume existing compiled outputs instead of rerunning the full platform bootstrap.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The new workflow invocations, their always-on PR conditions, and every transitive setup step are explicit in the YAML; the before/after job cardinality is exact. Only the magnitude of queue delay depends on cache size and available runner capacity, so severity is medium rather than high.
Findings.PerformanceResource: runner CPU plus checkout, cache-download/extraction, Electron-download, and filesystem I/O
Findings.PerformanceScaling: The duplicated setup grows with smoke shard count and PR concurrency: this change adds one full chat workflow on each of Linux, macOS, and Windows, plus a third full macOS proxy workflow, so every PR performs four extra platform preparations before executing the partitioned tests.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: substantially more runner-minutes and I/O per PR, reducing aggregate CI throughput and increasing queue pressure when PRs run concurrently
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Each platform had one Electron smoke job that performed checkout, dependency/cache restore, client and extension transpilation, Electron download, smoke compilation, and then ran the complete smoke suite; the macOS proxy tests reused that already-prepared job.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The added chat job invokes the same reusable Linux workflow as an independent job; analogous added macOS and Windows chat jobs and the macOS proxy job each independently repeat all unconditional preparation before running only their shard.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added `uses: ./.github/workflows/pr-linux-test.yml` at `.github/workflows/pr.yml:174` creates a second Linux smoke job. The same diff adds equivalent chat invocations for macOS and Windows and a separate macOS proxy invocation, while the reusable workflows unconditionally restore/extract node_modules, restore built-ins, run `transpile-client-esbuild transpile-extensions`, and download Electron for every invocation.
Findings.Title: Share smoke setup instead of rerunning the full platform workflow
Findings.Impact: On every PR, smoke coverage now launches two complete prepared environments per platform and three on macOS instead of one, even though each added environment runs only a complementary subset. This trades test wall-clock latency for a fixed four-job burst of duplicated CPU and I/O, which consumes shared/self-hosted capacity and lowers repository-wide CI throughput under realistic concurrent PR traffic.
Findings.Evidence: Tracing the added call into `.github/workflows/pr-linux-test.yml` shows that before the group-specific smoke command can run, every invocation performs an LFS checkout, node_modules cache download/extraction (or npm installs on a miss), built-in-extension cache access, full client/extension transpilation, and Electron download; because `smoke_tests` remains true, it also recompiles the common smoke extensions, smoke runner, and Copilot extension. The Darwin and Windows workflows have the same unconditional preparation. The grep/invert groups partition only Mocha execution, not this setup, so cache hits still repeat archive download/extraction and all compilation.
Findings.Recommendation: Preserve the shards but prepare the smoke build once per platform and have core/chat/proxy jobs consume that prepared artifact; if a shared artifact is not viable, keep the suites in one workflow until shard-specific jobs can skip the unrelated checkout/cache/build work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Electron smoke validation on every pull request, including core/chat shards and macOS network-proxy coverage
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each smoke check must finish a complete reusable platform workflow—checkout, dependency and built-in cache restore, full client/extension transpilation, Electron download, smoke/extension compilation—before its partitioned Mocha command can start. These setup boundaries are on every shard's critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Seven smoke workflow checkouts after the diff versus three before; four added per PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: One smoke workflow per platform checked out once; macOS proxy scenarios reused that workspace.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Every shard blocks on checkout before setup and tests.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Restore node_modules and built-in-extension caches, or install/download on cache miss
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Seven independent restore/extraction paths versus three before; on misses, the corresponding installs/downloads also fan out.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: One restore/install path per platform smoke job.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Each shard must obtain and extract dependencies before compilation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Full client/extension transpilation plus smoke and Copilot compilation
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Repeated once for each of seven smoke/proxy workflows versus three platform smoke workflows before.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: All smoke and macOS proxy tests reused one compiled workspace per platform.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Compilation completes before the shard-specific test process can start.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Location: Download Electron step in each reusable platform workflow
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Seven smoke/proxy workflow invocations versus three before, subject to underlying download caching.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: One Electron preparation served all smoke scenarios on each platform.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Electron preparation blocks every Electron smoke shard.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Run partitioned Electron smoke tests and macOS proxy scripts
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Core/chat test execution is partitioned rather than duplicated; two proxy invocations still run once each. Total test-case coverage is materially unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Core/chat tests ran in one process per platform, and both proxy scripts ran after the normal macOS smoke process in the same prepared job.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: This is the intended final work after setup; parallelization can reduce the longest individual check.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The effective cardinality is smoke shards per platform: one job per platform before the diff versus two on Linux and Windows and three on macOS after the diff. Core and chat Mocha execution is complementary through grep/invert, but preparation is not partitioned.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The new jobs run concurrently: two smoke preparations/tests on Linux, two on Windows, and three on macOS. There is no shared setup, sequencer, or backpressure between them; concurrent PRs multiply this fixed seven-job burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: On warm node_modules and built-in-extension caches, every shard still downloads/restores and extracts its own archives and recompiles client/extensions. On a cold cache, each shard can independently run npm installation and built-in downloads. Cache keys are platform/package-lock based and do not coalesce simultaneous restores. There is no negative cache.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the added reusable-workflow invocations and unconditional transitive setup steps are explicit, and before/after shard cardinality is exact.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact runner-minute increase and queue delay depend on cache archive size, compile duration, runner availability, and concurrent PR volume. The four added complete preparations and their placement are certain.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable repeated-work regression. Parallel test execution improves an individual PR's critical path, but the diff duplicates complete setup four additional times on every PR, reducing aggregate CI throughput.

Scenarios.Scenario: Agent Host E2E validation for changes classified as affecting the Agent Host
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A new classifier job first checks changed files. If affected, each platform's dedicated E2E job independently performs the complete platform bootstrap before starting the E2E runner; these jobs run beside the regular Electron integration jobs rather than reusing their already-prepared workspaces.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Checkout and GitHub pull-request file listing for classification
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One extra checkout and one paginated GitHub API operation on every PR. Previously detection called the API in three existing platform jobs, so API cardinality decreases from three to one while the checkout is newly allocated.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Detection ran after checkout inside each already-allocated Electron integration job.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: It gates only dedicated E2E jobs, not regular integration jobs.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Location: Dedicated calls at .github/workflows/pr.yml:153,218,294 into the reusable platform workflows
ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Platform checkout, dependency/built-in cache restore or install, and Electron download
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Three complete setup paths per affected PR, one per platform, added on top of the existing integration setups.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: E2E reused the corresponding integration job's checkout, dependencies, built-ins, transpiled output, and Electron download.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Every E2E platform check blocks on its own setup before tests.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Location: Unconditional `Transpile client and extensions` steps in all three reusable platform workflows
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Three additional full transpiles per affected PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The existing integration job transpile served E2E and all other integration suites together.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Directly precedes and blocks E2E execution.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Run Agent Host E2E suite processes
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Still one runner per platform and up to four child suites per runner; invocation count is not increased, but its concurrency now overlaps regular integration tests.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same platform suites ran from inside the integration jobs after setup.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Parallel placement shortens the longest Electron integration check but increases simultaneous runner demand.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One classification per PR. For affected PRs, three platform E2E workflows are added. The classifier's prefixes include broad build, base, and platform trees, so the effective trigger is wider than E2E-only changes.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The classifier serializes only the decision. Once true, three platform E2E jobs run concurrently with their three regular integration jobs. The E2E runner itself starts up to four suite child processes per platform, so up to twelve E2E children run concurrently in addition to integration workloads; worker count is bounded by suite count/available parallelism.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The classifier has no result cache. Dedicated jobs use the normal platform dependency caches, but warm hits still download/extract independently and do not reuse the integration jobs' workspace; cold misses independently install. Electron and built-in caches similarly do not coalesce across jobs.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the diff both skips E2E in the original integration jobs and adds three full reusable workflows, and the called workflows expose all unconditional boundaries.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: How often broad classifier paths are changed and resulting shared-pool queue delay are workload-dependent. The three added preparations on every affected PR are certain.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable repeated-work regression distinct from the smoke split. Moving tests parallel is intentional, but rebuilding all three platforms solely for E2E adds substantial fixed CI work and lowers aggregate throughput.

Scenarios.Scenario: Browser smoke, browser integration, and vscode-test-resolver server startup
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each harness spawns a VS Code server and waits for its endpoint. The added `--force-disable-user-env` reaches shell environment resolution and short-circuits login-shell probing before server readiness, reducing rather than adding critical-path work.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Spawn VS Code server and wait for endpoint
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Unchanged one server subprocess per harness launch.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same server subprocess was launched without forcing shell-environment resolution off.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Server readiness remains critical, but the changed argument removes a login-shell subprocess from startup.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve user environment through a login shell
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Previously potentially once per server process; now zero for these deterministic test servers.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Server startup could invoke shell environment probing when not otherwise disabled.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Removed from startup critical path by the added flag.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create temporary server data directory and logs
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing small filesystem setup remains before/around spawn.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Unchanged one process per resolver startup.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same server launch without the forced deterministic environment flag.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The added flag removes shell probing from server startup; it does not add a boundary.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Cost scales with server launches: each browser smoke launch in the automation harness, each browser integration browser/channel server, and each test-resolver authority server. The diff adds one flag per launch, not extra launches.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Existing harness concurrency and process ownership are unchanged. Browser/integration servers are spawned according to their existing runners; test-resolver startup remains one child process per resolution. No new queue or burst is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No new cache is introduced. The server uses the inherited deterministic CI environment; skipping user-shell resolution avoids repeated shell probing on both cold and warm launches.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: all changed arrays pass the recognized flag, and shellEnv explicitly returns early for it.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact time saved per launch depends on platform and shell configuration; no regression magnitude is uncertain because no expensive work was added.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. The change removes repeated subprocess work from deterministic test-server startup.

Scenarios.Scenario: Browser unit-test result reporting in CI
Scenarios.CriticalPath: For CI runs with `--tfs`, the browser runner attaches a console reporter and the unchanged JUnit reporter. The changed console reporter emits compact dots instead of full per-test spec lines while JUnit remains authoritative.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Format and write console progress for each test
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Unchanged event cardinality, but substantially fewer formatted characters/lines per test under Dot than Spec.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Spec formatted full suite/test titles and result lines for each test.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Reporter writes remain inline with test events but are reduced.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serialize full JUnit results to the test-results XML file
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Unchanged one JUnit result stream/file per browser runner.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical JUnit reporter and file path were already present.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Preserves full result detail and existing finalization work.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Console output scales with the number of browser tests. Both reporters observe the same runner; Dot emits compact progress while JUnit still serializes the complete result set once.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Reporter execution remains synchronous with Mocha events in each browser runner. Browser sequencing/parallelism is unchanged, and no extra reporter is added.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache participates. Output is regenerated per test run; JUnit file naming remains browser/platform/TFS-keyed.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: only the console reporter constructor changes; JUnit and runner topology are unchanged.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact CPU and log-upload savings depend on test count and runner logging behavior, but the changed mechanism cannot increase output work relative to Spec.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. This is a bounded serialization/output reduction.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 11 changed files. Submitted two medium-confidence findings at high mechanism confidence: smoke sharding repeats four complete platform preparations on every PR, and extracting Agent Host E2E repeats three complete platform preparations on affected PRs. Server environment flags and Dot reporting remove work and introduce no regression; smoke grouping itself partitions test execution without duplicating test cases.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
